findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the OAuth-App restriction is confirmed resolved before dispatch — name the concrete check (e.g. a navapbc org admin attests Third-party Access → the mcp-publisher device-flow app is approved, or a dry-run `mcp-publisher login github` + a non-mutating namespace check shows `io.github.navapbc/*`), the owner who has admin:org scope, and what to do if that confirmation cannot be obtained before dispatch.
evidence: Plan Context: 'Mitigation: before dispatch, confirm that OAuth-App restriction is resolved so the manual fallback is usable if mcp_registry fails again post-publish.'

0.13.0 handoff comment (ticket hyperbolic-pernicious-drongo): 'This points to navapbc's GitHub OAuth-App org-access policy blocking the mcp-publisher device-flow app -- requires a navapbc org admin with admin:org scope to inspect/approve (Settings -> Third-party Access); could not diagnose or resolve this further without that access.'
ABSENCE: the plan names the precondition but gives no concrete probe/command/owner for confirming resolution before dispatch (auth precondition class: Partially-verified/Unverified, not Verified).
findings.finding: The stated pre-dispatch mitigation — 'confirm that OAuth-App restriction is resolved so the manual mcp-publisher fallback is usable' — is an external precondition the plan depends on but does not specify how to verify, and the 0.13.0 postmortem established that inspecting/approving the navapbc org OAuth-App access policy requires an org admin with admin:org scope that the release identity did not have.
findings.location: Context → 'Mitigation: before dispatch, confirm that OAuth-App restriction is resolved'; Plan bullet 1 ('confirm ... the navapbc OAuth-App access posture')
scenarios: mcp_registry fails again post-publish exactly as in 0.13.0; the operator reaches for the manual mcp-publisher fallback assuming the mitigation was met, but the OAuth-App restriction was never actually verified resolved and publish 403s on io.github.navapbc/* again.
The release identity cannot itself inspect the org's Third-party Access setting, so 'confirm resolved' silently degrades to an unchecked assumption.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a prerequisite step: have a navapbc org admin (admin:org) verify Settings → Third-party application access shows the mcp-publisher OAuth App approved, OR perform a pre-dispatch `mcp-publisher login github` and confirm the returned namespace claims include io.github.navapbc/* (not just io.github.<user>/*). If neither can be confirmed, treat the registry AC as accepted-exception up front (file the follow-up before dispatch) rather than discovering the block post-publish.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish the CI `mcp_registry` `github-oidc` path (primary, unaffected by the OAuth-App restriction) from the manual `mcp-publisher login github` device-flow fallback (the only thing the 0.13.0 OAuth-App block affected); make the OIDC job the expected success path given the description fix already landed, and scope the OAuth-App mitigation to the fallback only.
evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:455 `run: ./mcp-publisher login github-oidc` — CI path is workflow-OIDC, not device-flow
docs/releasing.md:443-455 describes mcp_registry as OIDC ('login github-oidc') with manual `mcp-publisher login github` only as a fallback

0.13.0 ticket handoff comment: the 403 / OAuth-App restriction was hit on the MANUAL `mcp-publisher login github` device flow; the CI job's own failure was the 190>100 char description (since fixed to 97 chars, commit af915ac63bb1)
0.13.0 redispatch failed at PyPI `400 File already exists`, so the fixed-tree OIDC mcp_registry job was skipped, never actually exercised against a live fresh publish
findings.finding: The plan's MCP-registry risk mitigation targets the wrong mechanism: it treats the navapbc OAuth-App restriction (which the 0.13.0 ticket says blocked only the MANUAL `mcp-publisher login github` device-flow fallback) as the load-bearing risk, but the primary CI `mcp_registry` job authenticates via `mcp-publisher login github-oidc` — a distinct workflow-OIDC path authorized by running in navapbc/rebar and not subject to that OAuth-App restriction. The actual 0.13.0 CI failure was the server.json description-length bug (now fixed/landed), after which redispatch died on PyPI immutability before the OIDC job ever ran against a successful publish. A fresh 0.13.1 publish likely lets the OIDC job succeed on the first dispatch, so the manual-fallback mitigation and the pre-emptive [known-blocked-risk] framing may be aimed at a blocker that never recurs.
findings.location: Context 'Known risk'/'Mitigation'; Plan bullet 1; AC line '[non-codebase, known-blocked-risk] MCP Registry reports ... 0.13.1 as isLatest'
scenarios: Fresh 0.13.1 dispatch: publish succeeds to a fresh PyPI slot, mcp_registry OIDC job runs with the already-fixed 97-char description and publishes cleanly — the OAuth-App 'mitigation' was never on the critical path
Operator, following the plan, blocks/gates the whole release on resolving an org-admin OAuth-App issue that the CI OIDC path does not actually depend on
findings.suggested_fix: Rework the Known-risk/Mitigation to: (1) note the CI mcp_registry job uses `mcp-publisher login github-oidc`, whose namespace authorization comes from the workflow running in navapbc/rebar and is not the device-flow OAuth App that was blocked; (2) state the expectation that, with the ≤100-char description already landed, a fresh 0.13.1 dispatch's OIDC mcp_registry job should publish on the first run; (3) keep the OAuth-App/manual-fallback check as a contingency to exercise ONLY if the OIDC job fails, rather than a pre-dispatch gate; (4) keep the [known-blocked-risk] exception on the MCP AC but tie it explicitly to 'OIDC job failed AND fallback blocked', not to the OAuth-App posture alone.
